skin-only-facelift.text: Users consider it the simplest facelift, with milder recovery, for tightening loose facial skin and softening jowls and sagging. The skin tightening is visible once healed. The surgical literature compares it with deeper SMAS and deep-plane techniques, which are described as longer-lasting.

chain: Excess lid skin and fat removed
upper-blepharoplasty.text: Used to remove hooded or drooping upper-lid skin so the eyes look more open and rested, with the scar hidden in the natural crease. The visible change is the surgical result itself. Evidence for appearance outcomes is mostly surgeon-reported.

fat-repositioning-tear-trough.text: Users choose it to soften under-eye bags and the tear trough hollow together by relocating fat instead of removing it. The smoother lower lid is visible after healing. Support comes from surgeon case series rather than randomised trials.

co2-laser-blepharoplasty.text: Promoted as a way to get the same eyelid reshaping with a laser, sometimes combined with resurfacing of fine wrinkles around the eyes. Small studies report less bleeding and bruising during recovery, with a similar final look.

chain: Sutures bind lid skin to deeper tissue
double-eyelid-suture-non-incisional.text: Used mainly by people who lack an upper-lid crease to create a double eyelid without an incision, with a quick procedure. The new crease is visible straight away. Reports describe the crease sometimes fading over time.

le-fort-i-osteotomy.text: A major jaw operation used to correct bite and upper-jaw position, and discussed in looksmaxxing circles for reshaping the midface. Moving the maxilla visibly changes projection and proportion. It has a large clinical literature, mostly on function rather than looks.

t-osteotomy-genioplasty-mini-v-line.text: A Korean chin-bone surgery sought to narrow the chin toward a V-line shape and, in many descriptions, lengthen it. The reshaped chin is visible once swelling settles. Evidence is surgeon case reports rather than trials.

surgery-first-orthognathic-approach.text: Used by people planning corrective jaw surgery who want the facial change earlier, without a long pre-surgical braces phase. The jaw repositioning itself changes face shape. Cohort studies report treatment-time and stability findings that vary.

custom-peek-jaw-implant.text: A made-to-fit plastic implant discussed for building up or reconstructing the jaw for a more defined contour. The added contour is visible once healed. PEEK is established in spine and skull surgery, while cosmetic jaw studies have not been located.

maxillary-distraction-osteogenesis.text: A bone-stretching technique for advancing a recessed upper jaw gradually, sometimes discussed for midface projection. The advancement is visible in the face. It is studied mainly in cleft and severe hypoplasia cases rather than cosmetic use.

mandibular-distraction-osteogenesis.text: A bone-stretching technique that lengthens the lower jaw gradually, discussed in hardmaxxing circles for a longer, more projected jaw. The lengthening is visible in profile. It is well documented in children with congenital conditions and unstudied for purely cosmetic use.

total-maxillary-osteotomy.text: Classed in looksmaxxing culture as a hardmaxxing procedure, it repositions the whole upper jaw to treat long-face problems and under-grown upper jaws. The change in facial structure is visible. The surgical literature is solid but has little on looks outcomes.

chain: Porous implant placed on chin bone
medpor-chin-implant.text: Used to add chin projection and balance a recessed profile, with tissue growing into the porous material to anchor it. The added projection is visible. It is an established option with little comparative trial data.

chain: Added chin, lip or nose volume
eptfe-gore-tex-facial-implant.text: A Gore-Tex-type implant used to add volume to the chin, lips, nasolabial folds and nose. The added contour is visible once healed. Cosmetic studies are small and mostly older.

chain: Soft implant placed on chin bone
silicone-chin-implant.text: One of the most common ways to add chin projection, using a soft implant that can be removed easily. The profile change is visible straight away. Published evidence is mostly on complications.

chain: Chin or facial area built up
mersiline-mesh-implant.text: Named in a chin-augmentation reference as an alternative implant material, apparently corresponding to Mersilene polyester mesh. Its facial-augmentation use is mentioned only in passing, and cosmetic data are essentially absent.

mustard-otoplasty.text: A long-established ear-pinning technique used to set back prominent ears by creating a fold with stitches, without cutting cartilage. The pinned-back ear is visible once healed. Support is mostly retrospective series.

chain: Stitches link ear bowl to mastoid
furnas-suture-technique.text: An ear-pinning method for ears that stick out because of a deep bowl, often paired with the Mustardé technique. The set-back ear is visible after healing. Evidence is case series, with a known recurrence risk.

stenstr-m-technique.text: An ear-pinning procedure that scores the front of the cartilage so it folds back, used to correct prominent ears. The pinned result is visible once healed. It has been used surgically for decades and is supported by case series.

merck-stitch-otoplasty.text: A closed, minimally invasive ear-pinning method that reshapes the ear using stitches placed through tiny incisions. The pinned-back ear is visible after healing. It is documented, with little published outcome data.

incisionless-fritsch-otoplasty.text: An ear-pinning approach that avoids a skin incision by placing stitches with needles, sometimes with light scoring of cartilage. The reshaped ear is visible after healing. It is documented in publications from 1995 to 2009, with thin outcome data.

converse-wood-smith-otoplasty.text: An older cartilage-cutting ear-pinning method that builds a natural-looking fold for prominent ears. The corrected ear shape is visible after healing. Little modern human data has been located.

earlobe-reduction-repair.text: A minor procedure used to mend torn or split earlobes from heavy earrings or gauges, or to shrink oversized lobes. The tidier lobe is visible once healed. The literature is many technique papers and small case series.

ear-cartilage-molding-earwell.text: A non-surgical splint system for newborns with prominent, cup or lop ears, reshaping soft infant cartilage over several weeks. Studies report high correction rates when started in the first weeks. It is a newborn option and not used for adults.

corner-lip-lift.text: Used to lift downturned mouth corners, widen the mouth and make lips look fuller, often with an upper lip lift. The new mouth angle is visible. Evidence is surgeon case experience, and some surgeons advise against it to protect white lip length.

chain: Tube of ePTFE placed in lip
gore-tex-lip-implant-softform.text: A tubular Gore-Tex-type implant placed in the lip for permanent added volume, sold under names like Advanta, UltraSoft and SoftForm. The fuller lip is visible after healing. Sources reviewed describe it only briefly.

alloderm-lip-augmentation.text: Uses processed donor skin placed in small rolls in the lip to add size, or along the lip border to sharpen it. The added volume is visible once healed. Sources reviewed give only a short description and one 2000 paper title.

dermalogen-autologen.text: Injectable fillers made from human collagen, from the patient's own skin (Autologen) or donor tissue (Dermalogen), used to add volume to lips and soften lines. The filling is visible after injection. Sources describe short-to-moderate persistence.

mucomuscular-flap-lip-augmentation.text: A surgical lip enlargement that moves tissue from inside the mouth into the lip for more size. The change is visible once healed. The only source reviewed describes flaps generally as adding little volume and slight protrusion.

lip-plumper-capsaicin.text: A chili-based lip gloss, sometimes with menthol or cinnamon, used as a non-injectable way to make lips look fuller for a short time. The swelling is visible within minutes. The volume is brief and formal evidence is thin.
